_doc: What this adapter can actually enforce, in the four words core uses:
enforced, prefix-allowlist, prompt-only, pending. A profile that
*requires* a capability missing from the map below is refused rather
than run under a restriction that exists only in the prompt — see
`requires` in core/profiles.example.json.
Nothing here is a grant. It is a declaration of what the generated
--settings document and the launch flags are worth.
setup: Needs the Claude Code CLI on this machine's PATH (or BOARD_CLAUDE_BIN naming it), signed in to the account runs should spend. Model names are Claude Code's own (--model): a full name or an alias.

_doc: How this adapter may be inspected without a vendor binary, so core
can check conformance while still knowing nothing about any vendor.
`describe` is the command — argument list, run with this directory
as its working directory — that prints what this adapter would hand
its vendor for one launch, in the normalised shape
core/adapters/README.md documents. The adapter names its own
interpreter so core never guesses at one. `stubEnv` names the
variable that replaces the vendor binary, so `run` itself can be
executed end to end against a stub.
How a card's checked inputs reach a run (task 132). `delivery`
names the one route: `exact-read` is a read-only pinned copy granted
by one exact Read rule per file (AGENT_CONTEXT, hook_settings.py).
`representations` are the kinds of content the vendor's file-reading
tool consumes as content rather than as bytes: Claude Code's Read
tool reads text, images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP) and PDF documents.
Permission text is not proof the vendor honours it; the opt-in
develop/claude-access-smoke.py probe is.
Which --model names are one model (task 142): the full names this
adapter knows, and the aliases Claude Code resolves to one of them.
Core reads it only to tell an independent reviewer's model from the
implementer's; it is never a catalogue or an availability claim. A
name in neither list cannot be shown to be any particular model, so
an independent review that depends on it is refused rather than
assumed. A local adapter override may extend both lists.

unsupported.filesystem-sandbox: Claude Code's permission rules match tool inputs; they cannot confine a run's reads to a named set of files, and the shell it is granted is not sandboxed. A pinned context bundle is a guaranteed input, never a boundary on reading.
unsupported.network-policy: the CLI exposes no network boundary this adapter could set
